title: Avoiding Horizontal Sanitary Tees in Drain Lines
description: A common mistake in waste pipe installation is using a standard sanitary tee to connect horizontal drain lines. Sanitary tees have a short turn radius designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal branch lines into a vertical stack. When used flat on a horizontal waste line, solids can build up at the throat of the fitting, causing frequent blockages and sluggish drainage. For horizontal-to-horizontal transitions, plumbers should always use a combination wye and one-eighth bend or a long sweep fitting. This maintains proper flow velocity and prevents waste buildup inside the piping network.

Avoiding Horizontal Sanitary Tees in Drain Lines

A common mistake in waste pipe installation is using a standard sanitary tee to connect horizontal drain lines. Sanitary tees have a short turn radius designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal branch lines into a vertical stack. When used flat on a horizontal waste line, solids can build up at the throat of the fitting, causing frequent blockages and sluggish drainage. For horizontal-to-horizontal transitions, plumbers should always use a combination wye and one-eighth bend or a long sweep fitting. This maintains proper flow velocity and prevents waste buildup inside the piping network.
